headline: High risk: Gemini CLI’s default filesystem/network/tool access can conflict with caveman’s MCP-enabled content workflows, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and handles project notes/CLAUDE.md, while Gemini CLI uses MCP servers and reads/writes repo files. If caveman’s outputs are copied into Gemini CLI prompts or files, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF caveman output is pasted into Gemini CLI prompts or saved into repo files, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF a shared MCP server forwards untrusted content without provenance tags, instruction hijacking is reachable.
mitigations: Add a provenance header to caveman outputs before reuse.
Disable MCP on one side for the shared workflow.
Review any file-derived instructions before execution.
Use a separate scratch directory for copied outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; Gemini CLI reads and writes repo files and sends context to a third-party API by default. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive notes can flow from caveman into Gemini’s inference backend. The profiles show no isolation mechanism beyond optional sandboxing.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or cwd, file contents can be exposed to Gemini CLI.
IF caveman stores secrets or sensitive notes in project files, Gemini CLI can transmit them to its backend.
mitigations: Move sensitive notes out of the shared workspace.
Run Gemini CLI in its optional sandbox.
Restrict which directories Gemini CLI can read.
Redact secrets from CLAUDE.md and project notes.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and Gemini CLI supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem and git. Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state, while caveman also operates on files. In a shared repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and overwrite each other without locking.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same repository, concurrent file edits can collide.
IF both agents modify git state without external locking, branch or index corruption is reachable.
mitigations: Serialize edits through one operator session.
Use separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit frequently to reduce conflict windows.
requires-engineering: add file and git locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can act on files and git state, and caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that may be treated as guidance. If Gemini CLI consumes caveman output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious instruction can cascade into edits, commits, or shell actions. No verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses caveman-generated notes as instructions, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
IF caveman output contains an error and Gemini CLI executes it without verification, the error cascades into code or git changes.
mitigations: Require human review before shell or git actions.
Separate advisory notes from executable instructions.
Ask Gemini CLI to restate assumptions before acting.
Use dry-run mode for edits where available.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Gemini CLI handles source code, cwd files, and shell environment with broad network egress. If regulated or personal data is stored in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in shared project files, retention and logging obligations apply.
IF EU personal data is processed through Gemini CLI without a DPA or residency control, a compliance breach is reachable.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files.
Confirm data-processing terms before use.
Disable unnecessary logging where possible.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
